mn58:3.17: Lit: ‘an iron water-chestnut’, Trapa bicornis, (‘Ikiliya’ in Sinhalese) an edible nut having a tough two horned shell in the form of a miniature bull’s head. See the translator’s note also.
mn58:6.25: para. 7. ayosiṅghāṭaka—an iron tetrapod: (Ven. Ñāṇamoli’s original translation). The exact meaning is uncertain, but the general sense is clear from the context. P.T.S. Dict. says ‘perhaps an iron ring (in the shape of a square or triangle)’, which seems rather to ‘square the circle’.
mn58:8.6: To make clear what speech a Tathāgata speaks and does not speak: [1] untrue, unconnected with good, unwelcome — does not speak (e.g. lies spoken to harm others). [2] true, unconnected with good, unwelcome — does not speak (e.g. worldly ‘news’ which pains others to hear). [3] true, connected with good, unwelcome — speaks at the right time (e.g. a reprimand to a wrong-doer, or the statement about Devadatta). [4] untrue, unconnected with good, welcome — does not speak (e.g. flattery). [5] true, unconnected with good, welcome — does not speak (e.g. worldly matters which though true are unprofitable). [6] true, connected with good, welcome — speaks at the right time (e.g. teaching Dhamma and Discipline). The two permutations ‘untrue, connected with good, welcome’ and ‘untrue, connected with good, unwelcome’ are not considered, as they are contradictory.
